title: The Ledger of the Marlowe Estate
premise: True-crime podcaster Lior Okonkwo is hired by a nervous, well-paying client to investigate the Marlowe Estate before a murder that hasn't happened yet — a prediction the client claims comes from letters written decades ago by the estate's vanished heiress, Vivienne Marlowe. As Lior digs into the cold case everyone believes was closed, they uncover a family built on stolen identities and a living heir who has spent thirty years hiding in plain sight as the estate's groundskeeper. The 'future murder' is in fact a scheduled confession: on the anniversary of Vivienne's disappearance, the hidden heir intends to kill the man who erased her identity — unless Lior can expose the truth first. In the end, Lior chooses love against duty, helping the heir escape with their name restored rather than delivering them to justice.
about_author: Ada Pemberton is a former archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing estate papers and probate disputes before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the secrets families bury in paperwork, and lives quietly in a coastal town she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A client known only as 'Corvid' hires Lior via encrypted message to prevent a murder at the Marlowe Estate — a crime dated three weeks out. Lior, skeptical but broke after sponsorships dry up, accepts. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking exhaustion with a career built on other people's tragedies.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Arriving at the decaying estate under cover of researching an episode, Lior meets the staff: a brittle housekeeper, a lawyer who flinches at Vivienne's name, and the silent groundskeeper, Elias Wren. Emotional beat: unease deepening into fascination as the house feels staged, like a set dressed for something.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, intercut with podcast narration. Lior reconstructs the official story: Vivienne Marlowe drowned in 1994; case closed as accident. But the coroner's file has pages missing, and the drowning date matches Corvid's predicted murder date exactly. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt rekindled.

chapters.title: What the Groundskeeper Grows
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior interviews Elias, who tends a garden of flowers Vivienne once painted. He knows details no stranger should — the exact color of her studio door. Lior suspects him but feels an odd kinship instead. Emotional beat: suspicion tangled with unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: Letters from a Drowned Woman
chapters.summary: Elias's POV (unrevealed). Hidden chapters reveal someone receiving posthumous letters from Vivienne, each predicting events with impossible accuracy — including one describing a podcaster arriving to ask questions. Emotional beat: dread and devotion, as the letter-writer prepares to keep a terrible promise.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A skeleton surfaces in the drained lake — not Vivienne, but a man reported missing in 1994: the private investigator hired to find her. The case was closed over a body they never found. Emotional beat: vertigo, as every certainty collapses.

chapters.title: Identity Is a Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Records show Vivienne didn't die — she paid the PI to erase her identity, then killed him when he tried blackmailing her back. Someone else took up her letters afterward. Lior realizes Corvid may be inside the house. Emotional beat: cold clarity hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the predicted date, the lawyer gathers the heirs to announce selling the estate. Lior confronts Corvid — revealed as the housekeeper, Vivienne herself, alive and dying, planning to kill the lawyer who forged her death certificate and now profits from her erasure. Emotional beat: confrontation crackling with grief and fury.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With police minutes away, Lior must choose: record the confession that would make their career, or help Elias — revealed as Vivienne's son, raised in hiding — spirit his dying mother away. Lior deletes the recording. Emotional beat: agonizing choice resolved by compassion over ambition.

chapters.title: The Final Episode
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, framed as the last podcast episode. Vivienne dies free weeks later; the estate passes to Elias, who offers Lior the truth for the record — off air. Lior airs a different story entirely, keeping their secret. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, identity finally chosen rather than assigned.
